messages.content: i found a drawing i made when i was a child. it is simple, but i like looking at it.
what do you like about seeing it now?
i can remember how much i wanted the house in it to look real. the door is larger than the person.
you can see what you were trying to make, even though the size of the things is different from a real house.
i do not want to fix it. i like that it is how i made it then.
keeping it as it is can leave that part of the memory in the picture. you do not have to change it into what you would draw now.
can you write one sentence about that in my voice?
i want to keep this drawing as i made it when i was a child, even though i would make a different picture now.
use only what i said about the drawing, without adding what i would do now.
i want to keep this simple drawing as it is because i like looking at what i made when i was a child.
does that mean i cannot make a new drawing of the same house?
no. you can keep the old drawing and make a new one too. both can be pictures of the same house, even if they do not look the same.
just say that last idea more simply.
you can keep the old picture and draw the house again on another page.
i have two cups. one is red and one is blue. are both red?
no. only one is red. the other is blue.
can i say neither is green?
yes. from the color you gave for each cup, neither cup is green.
what does neither do there?
neither is green says that the red cup is not green and the blue cup is not green.
give a shorter explanation.
neither is green says no cup in that pair is green.
if i change the blue cup to a green cup, is neither is green still correct?
no. now one cup is green, so neither is green would be wrong.
are both green now?
no. one is red and one is green.
what could i say about both if they are on the table?
both cups are on the table.
why can both work for place but not for green here?
because both cups have the place you gave, but only one has the green color. with both, what you say needs to be true for each cup.
write a story about a father making a food list for his son. the first list should leave out a detail the son needs.

a father wrote bread and milk on a page and asked his son to bring them from the shop. his son looked at the list and asked how much milk to buy. the father had been thinking about the container he always bought, but his son did not know which one that was. they talked about how much milk the family needed and how much money the son had. the father added the size to the list before the boy left. the first list had been clear to the father, but asking a question made it useful for the person doing the task.
what did the son ask for?
he asked how much milk to buy.
did asking mean he could not read the list?
no. he could read the words but needed more information to do the task.
why was the money important?
it helped them choose what he could buy. knowing what the family wanted was useful, but they also needed enough money for it.
can you know what size he chose from the story?
no. the story says the father added a size, but does not give the size itself.
write a question the boy could ask about the bread too.
what kind of bread should i buy, and how much do we need?
finish with the father saying thank you for asking.
his father read the list again and said thank you for asking before leaving. the boy put the page with his money and went to the shop.
i need to leave a conversation because my train is coming. how do i say that without a long explanation?
i need to go now. my train is coming. it was good to talk with you.
what if we were only starting to talk?
you could say: i need to go because my train is coming. can we talk another time?
i do not want to ask for another time unless i know i have time later.
then leave that part out. i need to go now because my train is coming is enough to explain why you are leaving.
can i still thank them?
yes. you could say: thanks for talking with me. i need to go now because my train is coming.
only give one short sentence.
thanks for talking with me, but i need to go now.
why did you leave out the train?
you asked for one short sentence, so i kept the thanks and the need to go. i can keep the train instead if the reason is the part you want.
yes, keep the reason and leave out the thanks.
i need to go now because my train is coming.
i read four pages yesterday and three today. how many have i read over those two days?
you have read seven pages over the two days.
how many did i read today?
three pages.
if someone asks how much i read, should i always answer seven?
no. seven is right for both days together, but three is right for today alone. ask which time they mean if it is not clear.
explain that with the time first in each part.
over both days, you read seven pages. today alone, you read three.
now i read one of those three pages again. is that four different pages today?
no. you have read three different pages today, and one of them more than once.
can i say i read four pages if i count that page again?
yes, if you make clear that one page was read again. that is different from saying you read four different pages.
what is a clear short answer about different pages today?
i read three different pages today.
now only give the number for both days together, without adding the same page again.
seven pages.
join these with while: my mother cooked. i read at the table.
while my mother cooked, i read at the table.
does that mean i finished reading before she started cooking?
no. while puts the reading during the cooking. it does not say the reading was finished before the cooking began.
can i put the reading first in the sentence?
yes. i read at the table while my mother cooked.
does changing the order change who cooked?
no. your mother still cooked, and you still read. only the order of the parts in the sentence changed.
now make it about her reading and me cooking.
while i cooked, my mother read at the table.
if i use after instead of while, what changes?
after puts one thing later than the other. after i cooked, my mother read at the table says her reading happened after the cooking.
what if she read during the cooking and kept reading after?
then say both parts: my mother read while i cooked and kept reading after i finished.
only give the first sentence again.
while my mother cooked, i read at the table.
write a story about a child being asked to bring a container but seeing more than one choice. keep it simple.

a child was helping her aunt make dinner. her aunt asked her to bring the container from the shelf. the child saw a large one, a small one, and one with food inside. instead of taking the first she saw, she asked which container her aunt needed. her aunt said she wanted the small empty one for the rice. the child brought it and put it near the pan. her aunt had known which one she wanted, but had not given enough detail for the child to know too.
why did the child ask?
there was more than one container, and the request did not make the choice clear.
was it wrong for her to need more information?
no. she could read the request, but it did not tell her which container her aunt wanted.
make that explanation shorter.
she needed more detail, not help with reading.
what detail made the choice clear?
her aunt asked for the small empty container for the rice.
could the request be clear without saying what food it is for?
yes, if only one container was both small and empty. small empty container could be enough to choose it.
finish with the aunt giving a more clear request next time.
later, her aunt asked for the large container with food in it. this time, the child knew which one to bring.
a song came on while i was cleaning, and for a moment i stopped thinking about the work.
was it a song you already knew, or something new to you?
i knew it from a long time before. i had not thought about it for a long time.
hearing it again can bring back something you had not been thinking about. what did you remember first?
the first line. i knew what came next before i could remember the name.
you remembered part of the song before you remembered what it was called.
can you know when i first heard it?
not unless you tell me. knowing that you heard it long before does not give a specific day or year.
i do not remember either. i just liked hearing it again.
you can enjoy that without finding the first time you heard it.
write a short sentence about the moment, without giving a day or year.
i stopped cleaning for a moment when i heard a song i had not thought about for a long time.
now make it more about hearing the song, and leave the cleaning out.
i enjoyed hearing a song i knew but had not thought about for a long time.
